usage: This is the standard, everyday way to say I don't understand in Egyptian Arabic. It uses the active participle instead of a present tense verb, literally translating to I am not understanding. It is perfectly acceptable in both casual and formal situations across Cairo.

variants.label: female speaker
variants.note: This is the mandatory feminine form used when the speaker is a woman.

variants.label: past tense
variants.note: Use this conjugated verb form to say you didn't understand something that was just said.

variants.label: emphatic
variants.note: Use this when you are completely confused or lost in a conversation.

variants.label: group
variants.note: Used when speaking on behalf of a group of people.

responses.english: I will explain it to you.

examples.arabic: أَنَا مِش فَاهِم أَنْتَ قَصْدَك إِيه.
examples.english: I don't understand what you mean.

examples.arabic: مُمْكِن تِعِيد تَانِي؟ أَنَا مِش فَاهِم.
examples.transliteration: momken te3id tany? ana mish fahem.
examples.english: Can you repeat that? I don't understand.

examples.arabic: بِصَرَاحَة، أَنَا مِش فَاهْمَة الدَّرْس دَه خَالِص.
examples.transliteration: besara7a, ana mish fahma el dars da khales.
examples.english: Honestly, I don't understand this lesson at all.
